title: Execution Governance policy
description: Schema for eg-policy.yaml. This describes the shape a policy must have. It is NOT the whole contract: the engine additionally rejects a rule referencing an undeclared actionClass, and an argsPattern that is not a compilable regex. Neither is expressible here. `mcp-gate --validate` runs the engine's own parser and is therefore strictly stronger than validating against this file. Use this schema for editor completion and for CI on non-JavaScript toolchains; use --validate as the gate.

version.description: Recorded on every receipt as policyVersion. Omitted, the engine records "unversioned", which makes a receipt unable to say which policy produced it.

actionClasses.description: Named categories of risky behaviour, so rules read as intent rather than as globs.

tools.description: Tool-name globs, matched case-insensitively. * matches within one dot-separated segment, ** matches across segments.

argsPattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against JSON.stringify(args). Quote it in YAML so backslashes stay literal.

rules.description: Evaluated in order; the first match wins. A request matching no rule is DENIED. Order is therefore load-bearing: an allow placed above a deny will swallow it.

effect.description: The decision when this rule matches.

class.description: Name of an entry in actionClasses. The engine rejects a name that is not declared there; this schema cannot check that.

argsPattern.description: Additional case-insensitive regex filter over JSON.stringify(args).

reason.description: Recorded verbatim on the receipt. This is what a person reads when a call is denied, so write it for them.
